# Oaks Analysis

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
# read in data
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
# Clean height data for ANOVA
Height_Data <- Height_Data_Raw |> 
  select(Date, Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, Dead_Alive) |> 
# Rename columns
  rename(Tag = Tag_Num, 
         SaplingID = Sapling_AB_etc,
         Height = Seedling_Ht_cm, 
         Status = Dead_Alive) |> 
# Remove 'dead' saplings   
  filter(Status != "Dead")

Height_Data <- Height_Data |> 
  filter(Treatment != "NR")

# Change treatment class names which do not match 
Height_Data$Treatment[Height_Data$Treatment == "OA"] <- "OS"

# Checking classes of variables, changing to what they need to be for analysis
glimpse(Height_Data)

Height_Data$Treatment <- as.factor(Height_Data$Treatment)

Height_Data$SaplingID <- as.character(Height_Data$SaplingID)

Height_Data$SaplingID[is.na(Height_Data$SaplingID)] <- ""

# make sapling id uniform
Height_Data <- Height_Data |> 
mutate(SaplingID = if_else(SaplingID == "A", "A1", SaplingID)) |> 
  mutate(SaplingID = if_else(SaplingID == "B", "A2", SaplingID)) |> 
  mutate(SaplingID = if_else(SaplingID == "C", "A3", SaplingID)) |> 
  mutate(SaplingID = if_else(SaplingID == "", "A1", SaplingID))
```

```{r}
 # Clean SPAD data and combine with Height data for regression

SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> 
  select(Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6) |> 
  # remove NA rows
  na.omit() |> 

  # create mean SPAD column
mutate((SPAD_mean = rowMeans(pick(Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6), na.rm = TRUE)))

names(SPAD_Data)[10] <- "SPAD_mean"
  
SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data |> 
  filter(Treatment != "NR")
  
  # separate sapling number from tag number
SPAD_Data <- SPAD_Data |> 
  separate(col = "Tag_Num", sep = 3, into = c("Tag", "SaplingID"))

 # make sapling id uniform
SPAD_Data[SPAD_Data == "B"] <- "A2"
SPAD_Data[SPAD_Data == "A"] <- "A1"
SPAD_Data[SPAD_Data == ""] <- "A1"
```

```{r}
# Combine SPAD data with height data for regression

Height_SPAD <- inner_join(SPAD_Data, Height_Data, by = c("Block", "Treatment", "Tag", "SaplingID"))
```

## ANOVA

Does treatment influence height of Oak seedlings?

### Checking for Normality and Assumptions

```{r}
# assumption/normality tests

# visualizing height conductance across treatments 
ggplot(Height_Data)+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = Height)+
  geom_boxplot()

# exmaining height distribution
ggplot(Height_Data)+
  aes(x = Height)+
  geom_histogram()
# data is skewed towards the left, I will try log transforming 

ggplot(Height_Data)+
  aes(x = log(Height))+
  geom_histogram()
# looks better

# write the model 
anova_model <- lm(log(Height) ~ Treatment, data = Height_Data)

# checking q-q residuals
plot(anova_model, which = 2)
# the majority of the residuals follow the trendline, so I will continue

# shapiro test
shapiro.test(anova_model$residuals)
# W = 0.94451, p-value = 0.01216
# this indicates abnormality (p < 0.05) in the data, but this test is highly sensitive with large sample sizes so I will continue

# testing for homogeneity of variance 
plot(anova_model, 1)

# bartlett test
bartlett.test(log(Height) ~ Treatment, data = Height_Data)
# Bartlett's K-squared = 16.167, df = 2, p-value = 0.0003086
# p-value is low, indicating variance between treatments

Height_Data |> 
  group_by(Treatment) |> 
  summarize(Count = n())
# sample sizes are relatively even among groups, so I can ignore the assumption of homogeneity of variance 

```

### One-Way ANOVA and Post-Hoc Test

```{r}
# Running ANOVA

anova(anova_model)
# p = 0.01821

# TukeyHSD post hoc
tukey_res <- TukeyHSD( aov(log(Height) ~ Treatment, data = Height_Data) )
print(tukey_res)
# OS-AC = 0.01356367

tukey_df <- as.data.frame(tukey_res$Treatment)
tukey_df$Comparison <- rownames(tukey_df)
rownames(tukey_df) <- NULL

# Reorder so Comparison is the first column
tukey_df <- tukey_df[, c(5, 1:4)]
```

### Figure

```{r}

anova_summary <- Height_Data |> 
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(Height), 
            se = sd(Height)/sqrt(n())) 


anovaplot <- ggplot(anova_summary) + 
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean, fill = Treatment) + 
  geom_col() + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (mean - se), ymax = (mean + se)), width = 0.2)+
  annotate("text", x = .75, y = 37, label = "p = 0.0136", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5)+
  ylab("Mean Height (cm)")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Height of oak seedlings across treatments")+
  geom_text(label = c("A", "AB", "B"), 
            aes(y = 30, x = Treatment),
            vjust = 0, 
            size = 4.5)+ 
      ylim(0, 38)

tiff("anova.tif", width =4.5, height = 4, units = 'in', res = 300)
anovaplot 
dev.off()

```

### Table

```{r}

anova(anova_model)

anova_df <- as.data.frame(anova(anova_model))
```

## ANOVA II

### Checking for Normality and Assumptions

```{r}
# assumption/normality tests

# visualizing SPAD across treatments 
ggplot(SPAD_Data)+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = SPAD_mean)+
  geom_boxplot()

# exmaining SPAD distribution
ggplot(SPAD_Data)+
  aes(x = SPAD_mean)+
  geom_histogram()

# write the model 
anova_model2 <- lm((SPAD_mean) ~ Treatment, data = SPAD_Data)

# checking q-q residuals
plot(anova_model2, which = 2)
# the majority of the residuals follow the trendline, so I will continue

# shapiro test
shapiro.test(anova_model2$residuals)
# W = 0.9301, p-value = 0.1739
# this indicates normality

# testing for homogeneity of variance 
plot(anova_model2, 1)

# bartlett test
bartlett.test(SPAD_mean ~ Treatment, data = SPAD_Data)
# Bartlett's K-squared = 0.72012, df = 2, p-value = 0.6976
```

### One-Way ANOVA

```{r}
# Running ANOVA

anova(anova_model2)
# p = 0.5042

anova2_df <- as.data.frame(anova(anova_model2))
```

### Figure

```{r}
anova2_summary <- SPAD_Data |> 
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(SPAD_mean), 
            se = sd(SPAD_mean)/sqrt(n()))

anova2plot <- ggplot(anova2_summary) +
  aes(x = reorder(Treatment, mean), y = mean, fill = Treatment) + 
  geom_col() + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (mean - se), ymax = (mean + se)), width = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.75, y = 38, label = "p = 0.5042", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5)+
  ylab("Mean leaf greenness (SPAD)")+
  xlab("Treatment")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Leaf Greenness of Oak Seedlings Across Treatments")

tiff("anova2final.tif", width =6, height = 4, units = 'in', res = 300)
anova2plot 
dev.off()

```

## Regression

Is greater stomatal conductance associated with an increase in soil moisture for oak seedlings?

### Checking for Normality and Assumptions

```{r}

# I will see if there is a linear relationship between the two intended variables
ggplot(Height_SPAD) +
  aes(x = Height, y = SPAD_mean)+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

# making the model 
reg_model <- lm(SPAD_mean ~ Height, data = Height_SPAD)

#visualizing residuals

plot(reg_model, which = 2)
plot(reg_model, 1)

shapiro.test(reg_model$residuals)
# W = 0.94663, p-value = 0.4054

```

### Spearman's Rank Test

```{r}

# Is there a correlation between the variables?

spearcor <- cor.test(Height_SPAD$SPAD_mean, Height_SPAD$Height, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

spearcor$estimate
rho_spear <- round(spearcor$estimate, 4)

spearcor$p.value
round(spearcor$p.value, 4)
# rho = -0.0539, p-value = 0.8372
```

### Calculating Line of Best Fit

```{r}

summary(reg_model)

# making the vlaues into objects so that I can write the formula for the best fit line on the final figure
slope <- coef(reg_model)[2]
int <- coef(reg_model)[1]
p <- round(spearcor$p.value, 3)

slope <- round(slope, 3)
int <- round(int, 3)
rho_spear <- round(rho_spear, 3)

```

### Figure

```{r}

Reg_plot <- ggplot(Height_SPAD) +
  aes(x = Height, y = SPAD_mean)+
  geom_point()

Reg_plot <- Reg_plot +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", linetype = "dotted", se = FALSE) +
  geom_text(x = 40, y = 35,
            label = paste("Spearman's rho = ", rho_spear, "\n", "p = ", p, "\n", "y = ", slope, "x +", int)) +
  ylab("Leaf Greenness (SPAD)")+
  xlab("Height (cm)")+
  ggtitle("Oak Seedling Height vs Leaf Greenness")+
theme_classic()

tiff("reg.tif", width =4.5, height = 4, units = 'in', res = 300)
Reg_plot 
dev.off()

```
